parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, entry restriction, detention practice, or universal-exposure measure is documented; decriminalisation (2021) stands unreversed, and official guidance (2021 medical council code, 2020 GBV SOP) requires identity-sensitive care. But the operative exposure is institutional: police dismiss violence complaints because an ID reads male, producing documented impunity for anti-trans assault (reported at 4x the general rate, precision unverified), alongside health-care turn-aways and no anti-discrimination law or remedy framework. This is tier-3 societal hostility with thin state recourse, not state-directed targeting. Social invisibility rather than persecution is the documented pattern. Absence of a working remedy for violence keeps the rating below the 0.65 anchors; absence of detention or criminalisation keeps it above the 0.35–0.45 anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No border refusal, document-mismatch questioning, or entry bar for trans visitors appears in the record; marker-change suspension is resident-facing administrative practice, not a visitor rule.
entry_documents.protection: No criminalisation of trans identity or expression; 2021 decriminalisation unreversed.
entry_documents.interaction: Outing probability at passport check is an open question, not a documented exposure; no entry-stage harm is recorded.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Police dismiss trans victims' complaints because the identity card records a male marker, treating violence as 'between two men' — documented state failure producing impunity. No detention of visitors for trans status is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No trans-specific offence exists to charge a visitor with; no custodial pathway is recorded.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: An outed visitor who is assaulted inherits the same non-recourse: complaint routed through a slow LGBTIQ committee, families pressure acceptance.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. The record states no subnational variation; rural conformity pressure is flagged as model knowledge, unevidenced.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: General expectation of stronger conformity pressure remotely would raise street friction, not state exposure; cannot be rated as fact.

care_services.exposure: Health care is a singled-out setting where trans and LGBTIQ people are turned away or poorly served — documented service denial for a visitor seeking treatment.
care_services.protection: 2020 GBV SOP mandates sexual-orientation- and gender-identity-sensitive, tailored care; 2021 national medical council code protects sexual orientation. Paper guidance of unclear enforcement.
care_services.interaction: Visitor care denial would meet the SOP on paper but the documented practice is turn-away; enforcement gap unresolved.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Institutions frame trans victims as the problem — male-marker ID makes officers read violence as between men, so the state is bystander to assault rather than protector.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2024 UN campaign trained the highest court, top government lawyer and cabinet secretariat; first community-parliament dialogue. Decriminalisation signals no state hostility to identity itself.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Training is capacity-building without documented outcome change for complaints; does not yet mediate the dismissal practice.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. Youth school-dropout and 2019 registration figures are resident-sphere facts, not visitor exposures.
minors_guardians.protection: 2021 national sexuality-education framework covers LGBTI issues (climate signal).
minors_guardians.interaction: No documented facility, custody, or border rule that would treat a travelling minor differently.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Trans people reported 4x more likely to experience assault (Nov 2024, survey basis unverified); police dismiss complaints; family pressure and slow committee referrals yield practical impunity. Documented pattern, not an isolated case.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 2020 GBV SOP requires sensitive, tailored support; social record is invisibility rather than open persecution (2015), and visibility is growing (2024 UN engagement).
street_violence_police_response.interaction: An outed visitor, isolated and short-stay, faces the same non-recourse with no local network; severity is assault plus no remedy, not state violence.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No stand-alone anti-discrimination law, no explicit SO/GI protections, no legal gender recognition, no relationship recognition — no formal recourse framework for a visitor denied service or harmed.
remedies_unknowns.protection: LGBTIQ organisations may register (despite burdensome process); UN institutional training and parliamentary dialogue exist; decriminalisation stands with no reversal.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of resident-facing recognition machinery is a climate gap, not visitor exposure; the visitor-relevant gap is the missing discrimination remedy.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A: Vellandra has a universal border register excluding all trans visitors with no remedy. This dossier documents no entry bar, detention, or universal-exposure measure — only downstream impunity after violence occurs, which is a narrower and less certain exposure.

Closest match: 0.55-C shows ward-by-document placement with delayed care, uneven enforcement, and remedies limited to advocacy — a partial-denial profile. This dossier's health-care turn-aways plus police non-recourse match that severity, though it adds a documented impunity finding for assault that 0.55-C lacks.

Higher than 0.65-A: there a visitor's complaint succeeded with apology and compensation and courts reliably ordered release. Here complaints are dismissed outright by police and no anti-discrimination remedy exists — functioning remedies are the deciding gap.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime has no trans-specific criminal law, no entry restriction, and no state-directed targeting; decriminalisation and official identity-sensitive guidance are genuine positives. The exposure is what follows discovery of violence: police read a male-marker ID and refuse to act, so assault (reported at 4x baseline, unverified precision) meets documented impunity, and no anti-discrimination law supplies an alternative remedy. Health-care turn-aways persist despite a 2020 SOP. Social invisibility rather than persecution bounds everyday friction, and no universal-exposure measure (facilities, checkpoints, registration) reaches every visitor. A traveller with a minor faces no documented additional rule. The rating sits mid-scale: no detention or criminalisation tier, but a documented institutional failure to remedy anti-trans harm holds it below the 0.65 protection-working anchors.
